clue.text: Large lady giving offence — in double Dutch?

parts.note: large means big
Amy is a woman's name, standing for any lady

explanation.surface: A stout woman says something rude, perhaps in gibberish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double Dutch' looks like nonsense talk, but 'Dutch' is old slang for a wife, so a double Dutch is two wives at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Having two spouses at the same time is a criminal offence.

clue.text: Plants many a shrub inside spring frame

indicators.note: inside tells us the shrub goes within the other letters

parts.note: to bed plants is to plant them out, so plants means beds
D is the Roman numeral for 500, standing for many
the tea plant is a shrub

explanation.surface: A gardener sets out shrubs within a spring framework.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed's frame holds the springs and mattress, the framework of a bed.

clue.text: Explosive mixture, dominant in prison

indicators.note: in places the musical note inside the word for prison

parts.note: gaol is the British spelling of jail
soh is the fifth note of the scale, called the dominant in music

explanation.surface: Something volatile and powerful is locked up in jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A blend of petrol and alcohol used as motor fuel, which burns explosively.

clue.text: Teacher — mother ruffled his hair

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother

indicators.note: ruffled hair is messed up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mother tousles her son's hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu spiritual guru or sage, such as a teacher of meditation.

clue.text: Pink cheeks seen at a function in the Highlands

indicators.note: in puts the mathematical function within the Highland district

parts.note: Ross is a district of the Scottish Highlands, as in Ross and Cromarty
sine is a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: Ruddy faces are noticed at a social do in northern Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosy glow, the healthy reddish colour of the face.

clue.text: One or two in the team need an introductory guide

definitions.text: One or two in the team need an introductory guide

parts.words: One or two in the team need an introductory guide
parts.note: a cricket side sends out two players first to start, or guide in, its innings

explanation.surface: A few members of the squad want a beginner's handbook.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the pair of cricketers who start a side's innings at the crease.

clue.text: Small piece of land is assigned

parts.note: let means allotted or rented out, so assigned

explanation.surface: A small plot is allocated to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny island surrounded by water.

clue.text: Sign English note put into Norwegian

indicators.note: put into places the musical note inside the word for Norwegian

parts.note: Norse means Norwegian or Scandinavian
D is a musical note

explanation.surface: An English banknote is slipped into a Norwegian's hand for a signature.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse is to sign the back of a cheque or document.

clue.text: Scattered opponents after fight

indicators.note: after puts the opponents behind the fight

parts.note: to spar is to box or fight
in bridge, South and East sit at adjacent sides as opponents

explanation.surface: Rival forces disperse once the battle is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinly spread, few and far between.

clue.text: "… if it's only idle chatter of a ______ kind" (Patience)

definitions.text: "… if it's only idle chatter of a ______ kind" (Patience)

parts.words: "… if it's only idle chatter of a ______ kind" (Patience)
parts.note: a line from Bunthorne's song in the Gilbert and Sullivan operetta Patience, with one word left out

explanation.walkthrough: Patience is a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera mocking aesthetes; the missing word comes from the patter song 'If you're anxious for to shine'.
explanation.definitionFit: The lyric mocks lofty, mystical talk that rises above ordinary experience.

clue.text: Girl's price for performance

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, so girl's gives Di's
a charge is a price asked

explanation.surface: A young woman's fee for appearing on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrying out a duty is its fulfilment or execution.

clue.text: Daily riots in Asia Minor once

indicators.note: riots suggests disorder, so the letters of the preceding word are thrown about

explanation.surface: Disturbances break out every day in ancient Anatolia.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the answer rather than naming it: an ancient kingdom located in Asia Minor.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient kingdom in western Anatolia, ruled by Croesus.

clue.text: Trouble near the capital

indicators.note: to trouble is to disturb, so these letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: Unrest close to the seat of government.
explanation.definitionFit: An older spelling of Tehran, the capital city of Iran.

clue.text: Doctors' places in confinement

definitions.meaning: detains, especially in wartime, without trial

explanation.surface: Where doctors are kept during childbirth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confinement' suggests childbirth and the maternity ward; it is really imprisonment.
explanation.definitionFit: Junior trainee physicians, and also a verb for detaining enemy aliens.

clue.text: A sailor returns to the range

indicators.note: returns means the word for sailor is turned back to front

parts.note: an old salt is a seasoned sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman goes back to the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: The Atlas Mountains are a mountain chain in north-west Africa.

clue.text: Familiar name for undisciplined non-com, for example

indicators.note: undisciplined means out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nickname given to an unruly NCO.
explanation.definitionFit: A cognomen is a nickname or surname, originally a Roman family name.

clue.text: Dissipated, more than exhausted

parts.note: over means more than
spent means used up or exhausted

explanation.surface: Someone is wasted, utterly worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissipated money has been squandered, so too much has gone out.

clue.text: Mother sometimes held in deep respect

definitions.meaning: a Mother Superior is often given the title ... Mother
deserving reverence, the literal sense of the word

explanation.surface: Mum is sometimes greatly honoured.
explanation.definitionFit: A title for clergy and senior nuns, meaning worthy of veneration.

clue.text: Gunmen with one aim — a large estate in Spain

parts.note: HAC is the Honourable Artillery Company, a British army regiment
I is the Roman numeral one
an end is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: Armed men with a single objective target a big Spanish ranch.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacienda is a Spanish or Latin American landed property or plantation.

clue.text: Crichton wants to be the senior officer

indicators.note: wants means lacks, so the named letters are removed

parts.note: The Admirable Crichton is J. M. Barrie's play about a resourceful butler
taken as written

explanation.surface: A butler aspires to become the top-ranking officer.
explanation.walkthrough: Crichton is known from Barrie's play as 'the Admirable Crichton'; take BE from ADMIRABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest-ranking naval commander, a flag officer.

clue.text: Two less than the standard ten dollars once

definitions.meaning: in golf, a score of two strokes under par on a hole
a former US gold coin worth ten dollars

explanation.surface: Two short of the norm, worth a former ten-dollar sum.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer's two under par on one hole, and an obsolete American ten-dollar gold coin.

clue.text: Extra generous before parting

indicators.note: before puts the word for generous ahead of the extra

parts.note: good can mean generous or kind
a bye is a cricket extra, a run scored without the batsman hitting the ball

explanation.surface: Someone is especially kind before leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: A farewell said on leaving.

clue.text: Impulsive young officer assist, ing in plan

indicators.note: in places the junior officer within the plan

parts.note: a map is a plan or chart
ADC stands for aide-de-camp, a junior officer who assists a general

explanation.surface: A rash junior officer helps with a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A madcap is reckless and wild, acting on a whim.

clue.text: Cabinet member — one accepted by the aggregate

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body

indicators.note: accepted by places the numeral within the mineral word

parts.note: ore is rock, a natural aggregate of minerals
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A government minister is admitted by the whole body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cabinet member' looks like a minister, but 'Cabinet' alone is the definition, a piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: An armoire is a large wardrobe or cupboard.

clue.text: I severely criticize religion

parts.note: to slam is to criticise harshly

explanation.surface: Someone harshly condemns a faith.
explanation.definitionFit: The Muslim faith, revealed through Muhammad.

clue.text: A contraction in style, so in need of rewriting

indicators.note: in need of rewriting means the letters must be set down in a new order

explanation.surface: An abbreviation in prose so poor that it needs redrafting.
explanation.definitionFit: The contraction phase of the heartbeat.

clue.text: Sing for the king

definitions.meaning: to warble joyfully, especially a festive song
The name of two Romanian kings

explanation.surface: Perform a song for the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: To sing joyfully, and the name of King Carol I or II of Romania.

clue.text: Can be found in backward island city with skill

indicators.note: backward means the whole string of letters is read in reverse

parts.note: Elba is the island where Napoleon was exiled
EC is the postal district of the City of London
art means skill

explanation.surface: Something is discovered in a backwater city on an island, with talent.
explanation.definitionFit: Able to be tracked down or located.

clue.text: Game in the street with clubs

definitions.meaning: an old ball game like croquet played with mallets
a London street lined with gentlemen's clubs

explanation.surface: A sport played on the road with bats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clubs' suggests the mallets of the game; it is also the gentlemen's clubs of the London street Pall Mall.
explanation.definitionFit: Pall-mall was a mallet-and-ball sport, and Pall Mall a London thoroughfare famed for its clubs.

clue.text: Minister in residence at Ten Downing Street

indicators.note: in residence says the answer lives inside the following words, run together

explanation.surface: A government minister living at Number Ten, home of the Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' looks like a noun for the Prime Minister, but it is the verb: to minister to someone is to look after them. 'Street' is surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: To minister to someone is to serve or look after them.
